title: Sharper Committing-Security Bounds for EtE-HCTR2
summary: Known committing-security bounds for the two EtE-HCTR2 variants are tight up to a constant depending on n, but further optimization remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine sharper committing-security guarantees for $\mathrm{EtE}^{P}\text{-}\mathrm{HCTR2}$ and $\mathrm{EtE}^{S}\text{-}\mathrm{HCTR2}$, two variants of $\mathrm{EtE\text{-}HCTR2}$. The known committing-security bounds for both variants are tight up to a constant depending on $n$; the open task is to further optimize these bounds and their $n$-dependent constant.

scope.domain: Committing security of the EtE-HCTR2 cryptographic constructions.
parameters: n, the parameter on which the tightness constant depends
scope.unresolved_remainder: Further optimize the committing-security bounds for EtE^P-HCTR2 and EtE^S-HCTR2, including their n-dependent constant.

citations.label: Key Committing Security of HCTR2, Revisited

progress.summary: The source explicitly states that EtE-HCTR2 has open research problems in committing security. It identifies the two variants as tight only up to an n-dependent constant, with room for further optimization.
citation_labels: Donghoon Chang et al., Key Committing Security of HCTR2, Revisited
